title: How to See a Doctor
summary: Appointments, choosing a clinic and preparing for a consultation.

sections.heading: Before your appointment
sections.text: Ask the clinic about appointment availability, languages, fees and accepted insurance before you book. Bring your identification, insurance documents and a list of medicines you take. Ask your university for its verified medical-office details.

sections.heading: During your consultation
sections.text: Explain your concerns and ask questions if anything is unclear. Ask the clinician to explain prescriptions, how to take medicines and what to do if symptoms change.

title: Student Health Insurance Explained
summary: Understand compulsory and private cover, and know what to ask.

sections.heading: Compulsory medical insurance
sections.text: The Kyrgyz Compulsory Medical Insurance Fund (FOMS) publishes information for foreign students and describes compulsory policies. Its pages contain differing information about documentation, so confirm current eligibility, documents, price, effective dates and application steps directly with FOMS or your university.

sections.heading: Coverage and claims
sections.text: Ask which facilities and services are covered, what exclusions and co-payments apply, and how to register with a family medicine centre. If considering private insurance, compare emergency care, exclusions, reimbursement procedures and documentation. Keep copies of your policy and receipts.

sections.heading: Emergency treatment
sections.text: In an emergency, call 112 or 103 immediately. Confirm coverage and payment rules with FOMS or your insurer; do not delay seeking emergency help while checking paperwork.

sources.label: FOMS: foreign students and policy applications

title: Top Pharmacies and What to Buy
summary: Practical questions to ask when buying medicines.

sections.heading: At the pharmacy
sections.text: Ask a pharmacist whether a prescription is required and bring it when you have one. Do not assume that a particular medicine is in stock. Ask about generic and brand-name options and whether a proposed equivalent has the same active ingredient and strength.

sections.heading: Labels and storage
sections.text: Ask the pharmacist to explain the label, instructions and expiry date in a language you understand. Store medicines according to the label, away from children. Consult a healthcare professional if you are unsure.

title: Staying Healthy Through Bishkek’s Seasons
summary: Everyday considerations for weather, air quality, food and travel.

sections.heading: Everyday health
sections.text: For cold or flu symptoms, seek advice from a health professional if you are concerned. Wash hands regularly and follow local food and drinking-water guidance. Ask a clinician about seasonal allergies and persistent symptoms.

sections.heading: Air, winter and mountains
sections.text: Check local air-quality and weather information when planning outdoor activities. Dress for cold conditions. Before high-altitude travel, learn about altitude illness and plan a gradual ascent; seek urgent help for serious symptoms.

title: Mental Wellbeing
summary: Support for homesickness, academic stress and culture shock.

sections.heading: Finding support
sections.text: Moving and studying abroad can be stressful. Stay connected with trusted people, make time for rest and ask your university about counselling or student support. A qualified health professional can help you explore support that fits your needs. If someone is in immediate danger, call emergency services.

title: Cultural & Dietary Needs
summary: Discuss food, fasting and religious preferences with your care team.

sections.heading: Communicate your needs
sections.text: Tell your clinician about dietary restrictions, halal preferences and religious practices that matter to you. Ask about ingredients and alternatives when appropriate. If you plan to fast during Ramadan and have a health condition or take medication, discuss your individual circumstances with a clinician before changing your routine.
